post.description:
Routes the request to a task (a cited answer, practice questions, or the note assistant for a `selection`, which may propose inline edits) and starts a background job over the given scope. The scope is checked now and again on every search while the job runs; the server, never the model, decides what may be searched.

Routing: an explicit `command` always wins and costs nothing. Otherwise keyword rules and the surface default decide; when the optional AI router is enabled on the server it may decide instead, and for a near tie it returns 200 CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED with a closed set of options (no job is created). Show the options; resend the same text and scope with the chosen `command`, `clarified: true`, and a new Idempotency-Key.

Responses: 202 with `outcome: JOB` (follow it with GET /v1/ai/jobs/{jobId}/events), or 200 with `outcome: CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED`.

Idempotency: a retry with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the original job (`created: false`) without routing or charging again; the same key with a different body is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Use one key per user action and reuse it only for retries of that action.

Spend: the job is charged to the user’s daily AI allowance as it runs; if the allowance runs out the job fails with AI_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED (see GET /v1/ai/allowance). Rate limited per user.

Durability: the job runs on the server whether or not the client stays connected. Keep the job id, but if it is lost, GET /v1/ai/jobs lists the user’s jobs; finished ones the user has not opened have `seenAt: null`.

Web: `webSearch: true` lets a cited answer also search the public web, when the server has a web vendor configured. Web search runs only while the job’s data may go to that vendor, and never sends the learner’s material.

Research papers: add `webScope: "papers"` (the `/research` command) to search research papers instead of the web. Paper results carry `citations[].paper` (authors, year, venue, DOI, open PDF). The server picks the vendors and enforces shared rate limits; when search is busy or its free daily allowance is used up, the answer comes from the learner’s material and tool activity shows `AI_WEB_RATE_LIMITED` or `AI_WEB_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED`. Never retry the job for that.

info.title: Incantly API
info.description:
Frontend integration guide

This is a private developer reference, not an application login page. The documentation password must never be embedded in browser code or NEXT_PUBLIC variables. Try-it-out is disabled to prevent accidental writes and bypassing the auth forwarding boundary.

Health endpoints use the backend origin. Authentication endpoints must be called on the public web origin through /api/auth/*, using the Better Auth client and cookie credentials. The web server signs client identity for the backend; never create that signature or expose AUTH_PROXY_SECRET in a browser. Documentation credentials do not authorize API operations.

Email signup/login is passwordless. Request a six-digit OTP, then submit email and OTP; collect the display name for first signup. Codes expire in five minutes, permit three wrong attempts, and rotate on resend. Google uses sign-in/social and the configured callback. Account creation requires identity proof. Sessions use HttpOnly cookies. Never store session/OAuth tokens in localStorage or IndexedDB. JSON session tokens are removed by the backend response adapter even if generic SDK schemas mention them.

Send JSON for POST requests and preserve the exact allowed Origin and cookies. Auth JSON bodies are limited to 16 KiB. Callback URLs must match the configured origin allowlist. On 429 respect Retry-After; do not retry OTP submission blindly. Infrastructure failures return 503. UNTRUSTED_PROXY (403) means the request bypassed the trusted web entry point; UNTRUSTED_ORIGIN (403), INVALID_JSON (400), BODY_TOO_LARGE (413), RATE_LIMITED (429), and AUTH_UNAVAILABLE (503) are stable adapter codes. SDK errors remain intact.

Do not trust client-provided roles or IDs. Session identity does not replace note or asset ownership checks. Notes endpoints support immutable checkpoints, revisions, restore, deletion, trash and retention windows, and typed transaction synchronization; IndexedDB input is always untrusted. Asset endpoints support direct MinIO/R2 upload reservations, verified completion, short-lived downloads, abort, and retention-aware deletion. Presigned URLs are credentials: never persist or log them. Library Sources, Spaces, Note context bindings, and Context preview cover the study material the AI may use. AI endpoints (/v1/ai) create background jobs (a cited answer, practice questions, or the note assistant for selected text) over an explicit scope: submit with an Idempotency-Key, poll the job's events until done, then read the result and its cited passages; a near tie between tasks returns CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED with a closed set of options. AI text and passages are untrusted: render as text or sanitized Markdown, never raw HTML. Daily AI spend is capped per user (AI_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED). The note assistant may propose inline edits (/v1/notes/{noteId}/proposals): nothing changes until the owner accepts a change, which becomes an ai-origin revision that can be undone. Sharing endpoints manage grants, invitations, share links, and shared-with-me; Liveblocks endpoints authorize rooms and report live status; comments and notifications cover threads, inbox, preferences, and unsubscribe. Billing and tenant/team APIs are not implemented yet. Generated users scaffolding is not a supported product API and is intentionally excluded. Public health probes have no credentials or parameters. New endpoints must document schemas, examples, auth, stable errors, side effects, retry/idempotency rules and limits beside the implementation.

filename.description: Original file name, for display and downloads only; control characters and slashes are replaced.

contentType.description: The file’s MIME type. Other types return 422 ASSET_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED. The server verifies the uploaded bytes; a mismatch quarantines the asset.

byteLength.description: Exact size in bytes (max 250 MiB). Above 16 MiB the upload is multipart.

checksumSha256.description: Optional SHA-256 of the bytes, single uploads only (422 CHECKSUM_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_MULTIPART otherwise). When given, storage rejects different bytes.

items.description: Up to 50 files (2 GiB in total), for example a dropped folder. Same rules per file as POST /v1/assets/uploads.

url.description: Presigned storage URL. A credential: never persist, log, or share it.

headers.description: Send exactly these headers with the PUT (for example Content-Type).

expiresAt.description: Finish the upload before this (15 minutes).

index.description: Position of the file in the request.

status.description: HTTP status the single-file endpoint would have returned.

code.description: Stable code for a rejected file, e.g. ASSET_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED or IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.

entityTag.description: The ETag response header storage returned for this part.

parts.description: Multipart uploads only: every part number with its ETag. Omit for single uploads.

url.description: Five-minute private URL. Use it immediately; never store or log it.

sourceAssetId.description: A READY asset the user uploaded (text/plain or text/markdown, UTF-8, up to 10 MiB).

targetNoteId.description: Append the imported paragraphs to this Note; omit to create a new Note.

status.description: Poll every 2–5 seconds until completed, failed, or cancelled.

targetNoteId.description: The Note that receives (or received) the import.

errorCode.description: Stable failure code when status is failed.

url.description: An https URL the user entered. Private, local, and non-HTTPS addresses are refused.

roomId.description: The authoritative Liveblocks room ID. Always re-read it: rotation changes it.

checkpointHealth.description: Checkpoint health, present for the note owner only. `quarantined` means recent room changes failed validation and the head did not advance.

roomSizeBytes.description: Tracked Yjs room size in bytes, once checkpointed.

roomSizeWarning.description: True once the room reaches the 6 MB warning threshold.

canEdit.description: Whether the caller may edit this note. Viewers must open read-only and never submit.

currentRevisionNumber.description: The head revision number; send it as baseRevisionNumber when saving.

collaboration.description: Present on shared notes (notes with a live room).

avatarUrl.description: Stable avatar URL, never a presigned object URL.

purgeAt.description: When the note becomes eligible for the permanent purge (deletedAt plus NOTE_RETENTION_DAYS). Restore before then; afterwards the row and its checkpoints are gone.

origin.description: `ai`: an agent proposal change the owner accepted, or its undo. Show it as "Edited by AI, accepted by you". `collaboration`: a checkpoint of a shared note's live room; list its contributors.

versionName.description: User-named version label from POST checkpoints, when the revision has one.

document.description: The canonical Incantly JSON document, already validated by the server.

baseRevisionNumber.description: The revision number your document was edited from (the current head). A stale value returns 409 STALE_NOTE_REVISION.

document.description: The complete canonical Incantly JSON document (`@incantly/canvas-core`), never Tiptap JSON or HTML. Its `id` must equal the note ID; node IDs must stay stable across edits.

transactionId.description: Durable idempotency identity of this batch. Retry with the identical ID and payload; never reuse it for different operations.

clientId.description: Stable ID of this browser/device install.

tabSessionId.description: Per-tab session ID (same-browser tabs share a clientId). Scopes conflict recovery; omit for non-browser writers.

localSequence.description: Per-client increasing sequence, as a decimal string. Reusing one returns 409 CLIENT_SEQUENCE_REUSED.

baseRevisionNumber.description: The head revision the operations were made against.

sourceRevisionId.description: The revision to restore, from GET /notes/{noteId}/revisions. Omit it to restore a soft-deleted note from the trash instead: the note returns to live, its grants keep working, and its room access is re-mirrored.

name.description: Optional name for a user-named version. Validated, persisted on the new revision, and echoed; echoed only when the room is unchanged.

checkpointCreated.description: False when the room was unchanged since the last checkpoint: the head revision is returned as-is.

providerVersion.description: Whether the provider safety-net version was created. A provider outage reports false without failing the save.

versionName.description: Echo of the requested version name.

document.description: The client-held canonical Incantly JSON document after offline loss. Its `id` must equal the note ID. It is migrated, validated and authorized, then stored as a separate recovered revision: never applied over the room.

headUnchanged.description: Always true: recovery never moves the head. Re-apply the content through transactions.

failureCode.description: Stable failure code, e.g. CANCELED_BY_USER or INVALID_UTF8.

searchReadiness.description: NONE: not searchable yet. KEYWORD: keyword search works (the agent can already answer from this file). FULL: meaning-based search too. Enable "ask about this file" from KEYWORD.

embeddedPassageCount.description: Passages embedded so far; with passageCount, a progress bar from KEYWORD to FULL.

index.description: Search-index readiness; null for archived Sources.

canRetry.description: A retry would do something now.

kind.description: FILE needs assetId (text, Markdown, or PDF). AUDIO_TRANSCRIPT needs an audio assetId and transcriptionConsent: true. YOUTUBE_TRANSCRIPT needs a caption-file assetId (WebVTT or SubRip) and youtubeUrl. WEB_PAGE needs url. NOTE_REVISION needs noteRevisionId; PASTED_TEXT needs text.

assetId.description: A READY Asset you own, from a completed upload.

noteRevisionId.description: An immutable revision of a Note you own.

text.description: Plain text for PASTED_TEXT, at most 524288 UTF-8 bytes. Stored privately; never logged.

url.description: HTTPS page for WEB_PAGE. The API never fetches it: it is sealed and fetched by the isolated import boundary. Fails with 409 REMOTE_IMPORT_UNAVAILABLE where that boundary is not deployed.

youtubeUrl.description: YOUTUBE_TRANSCRIPT video (watch, youtu.be, shorts, or embed URL, or the 11-character ID). Used for provenance and timestamp links only; never fetched.

transcriptionConsent.description: AUDIO_TRANSCRIPT only, and required true: the user confirms they may record and transcribe this audio. The consent time is stored on the version.

spaceIds.description: Active Spaces to link in the same transaction. Any invalid Space rejects the whole command.

coverage.description: Share of the recording covered by transcript timestamps.

host.description: WEB_PAGE host only; the full URL is never returned.

documentTitle.description: Title declared by the document; untrusted display text.

processingStage.description: Set while PROCESSING. QUEUED_FOR_PROCESSOR, FETCHING, PARSING, TRANSCRIBING, and NORMALIZING belong to the PDF, web, caption, and audio processors. AWAITING_PROCESSOR means no processor exists for this media type (images: OCR is not offered); versions parked there before processors shipped can be retried.

partialReason.description: Why a PARTIALLY_READY version is incomplete: PDF_PAGE_LIMIT (only the first pages were parsed) or WEB_CONTENT_LIMIT.

assetId.description: The Asset behind this version, for opening a PDF at a cited page or seeking audio to a cited time.

youtubeVideoId.description: YOUTUBE_TRANSCRIPT video ID for timestamp deep links.

versions.description: Newest first. Lists return the latest version; reads return up to 25.

items.description: Up to 50 Sources, for example one per file of a folder upload. Same rules per item as POST /v1/library/sources.

index.description: Position of the item in the request.

status.description: HTTP status the single-item endpoint would have returned.

code.description: Stable code for a rejected item, e.g. ASSET_NOT_FOUND or SPACE_SOURCE_LIMIT_REACHED.

revisionPolicy.description: TRACK_LATEST resolves to the newest ready version when a job starts. PINNED_VERSION always uses pinnedSourceVersionId.

pinnedSourceVersionId.description: Required for PINNED_VERSION; must be a READY or PARTIALLY_READY version of this Source.

created.description: False when an identical active binding already existed.

scope.description: SELECTION: noteId + nodeIds. NOTE: noteId (plus its context bindings). SELECTED_SOURCES: sourceIds. SPACE: spaceId (+ includeSpaceNotes). CUSTOM: noteIds and/or sourceIds. LIBRARY: every usable Note and Source; use only after the user explicitly chooses broad search.

type.description: PAGE: a PDF page. TIME: a media range (audio, or YouTube when youtubeVideoId is set). BLOCK: a Note node or text block (use blockId).

blockId.description: Note node ID or normalized Source block ID.

sourceKind.description: Source kind (FILE, WEB_PAGE, ...); null for Notes.

assetId.description: Asset behind a PDF or audio Source: open it at `locator.page` or seek to `locator.startMs`.

evidenceId.description: Opaque citation ID within this manifest.

degraded.description: True when semantic search was skipped for some content (embeddings pending or provider unavailable). Keyword search still ran.

stale.description: Some requested content changed after it was indexed.

sensitivity.description: Highest data classification among the returned evidence (Notes count as PRIVATE). RESTRICTED evidence is never sent to an external AI provider.

searchReadiness.description: NONE: not searchable. KEYWORD: keyword search works. FULL: semantic search too.

building.description: A newer version is being indexed.

indexedVersion.description: Note revision number or Source version number indexed.

replayedFailedBuild.description: True when a previously failed index build is being retried rather than a new one queued.

doi.description: Checked DOI (10.x/...). Show as text; do not build links from it.

arxivId.description: Checked arXiv ID. Show as text; do not build links from it.

pdfUrl.description: An open PDF of the paper, checked to be http(s) without credentials. Link it only from here (rel="noopener noreferrer").

ref.description: The reference the model used, e.g. `S1E2` (search 1, evidence 2).

manifestId.description: The retrieval manifest holding the evidence.

page.description: PDF page, when the evidence is from a paged Source.

startMs.description: Start offset in milliseconds, for audio and video.

kind.description: `web` for W1R2-style refs (a web result); absent on older library citations.

url.description: Web citations only: the page URL as the vendor reported it, checked to be http(s) without credentials. Make it a link only from here (rel="noopener noreferrer"), never from URLs in the answer text.

title.description: Web citations only: the page title (plain text).

paper.description: Research-paper citations only (webScope `papers`): paper metadata. The only links are `url` and `paper.pdfUrl`.

answer.description: The answer. Plain text written by the model from the learner’s material (and web results when opted in); render it as text, or sanitized Markdown with images disabled and no remote content loaded, never as raw HTML. Show links only from `citations[].url`; render any other URL in the text as plain text, because untrusted web content could have planted it to leak data.

sufficiency.description: NOT_FOUND means the material does not answer the question: show that, and suggest adding Sources or widening the scope.

answer.description: The assistant’s reply; untrusted text (render as text or sanitized Markdown).

proposalIds.description: Edit proposals it stored for this note: load GET /v1/notes/{noteId}/proposals and draw them inline. Empty when it only answered.

kind.description: What the assistant may search. NOTE: one Note and the Sources bound to it. SPACE: a Space’s Notes and linked Sources. SELECTED_SOURCES: only the listed Sources. LIBRARY: everything the user owns; send it only after the user explicitly chooses a library-wide search.

sourceIds.description: Required when kind is SELECTED_SOURCES (1–50 IDs).

nodeId.description: The block (canonical node ID) the selection touches.

from.description: Start offset in the block’s text, in UTF-16 units as in `replaceText`.

revisionNumber.description: The note revision the editor shows.

surface.description: Where the user asked. Only changes the default task.

text.description: What the user typed, as plain text. Sent to the AI provider; never put secrets in it.

command.description: An explicit task from a UI control (for example a "Quiz me" button), or the option the user picked after CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED. When present, no classifier runs and nothing is charged for routing. `ask` and `answer.grounded` mean a cited answer; `practice` and `study.practice` mean practice questions; `edit` and `note.assist` mean the note assistant (NOTE scope only), which may propose inline edits.

clarified.description: Set to true when resending after CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED (together with `command`). The server never asks twice.

webSearch.description: Let the assistant search the public web for this request, when the server has web tools enabled. Off by default: show it as an explicit choice ("Search the web too"). The question, never the learner’s material, may be sent to the web vendor; web results are cited as W1R2-style refs.

webScope.description: What web search looks for, when `webSearch` is true: `web` for the `/search` command, `papers` for `/research` (research papers with authors, year, venue, and open PDFs). Ignored without `webSearch: true`. The server chooses the vendors; never send one.

selection.description: Text the user selected in the note editor: block IDs and offsets, never the text itself (the server reads it). Needs `scope.kind: NOTE`. Without a `command` it selects the note assistant, which may answer and may propose inline edits (GET /v1/notes/{noteId}/proposals).

command.description: Send this back as `command` with `clarified: true`.

description.description: Server-written description; safe to show as a choice.

options.description: A closed set of choices. No job was created.

id.description: The Note or Space; null for several Sources or the library.

status.description: ACCEPTED and RUNNING (and WAITING) are in progress; COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, and EXPIRED are terminal.

result.description: Only when COMPLETED: GroundedAnswerResult for agent.grounded_answer, PracticeQuestionsResult for agent.practice_questions, NoteAssistResult for agent.note_assist.

failureCode.description: Only when FAILED or EXPIRED. See the error table in the frontend guide (e.g. AI_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED, AI_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN, AI_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE).

deadlineAt.description: The job stops (EXPIRED) if not finished by then. Waiting for an approval or an external tool moves it later.

stateVersion.description: Increases on every change. Send it with an approval decision to prove you saw the current state.

webAllowed.description: The request opted in to web search.

webScope.description: What web search looks for: the web, or research papers.

seenAt.description: When the user marked the finished job seen (POST …/seen).

resultWithheld.description: True when the job finished but the user no longer has access to what it was about: `result` is withheld.

taskClass.description: The task the request was routed to.

source.description: How it was chosen: your explicit command, a keyword rule, the surface default, or the AI router.

created.description: False when this Idempotency-Key was already used with the same request: the original job is returned and nothing new is charged.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next (older) page; null at the end.

seq.description: Increasing per job; use it as `after`.

type.description: Treat unknown types as progress and keep following; new types are added over time.

data.description: Small details only (step number, reason code, retry time, counts); never text, URLs, or IDs from your content. Safe to show to the job owner and to log. TOOL_STARTED: {step, callId, tool, effect}. TOOL_FINISHED: {step, callId, tool, effect, outcome, reason?, …counts}. `callId` pairs the two; `effect` is read | propose | write | external; `outcome` is ok | refused | failed; `reason` is a code when the outcome is not ok. Counts by tool (outcome ok): read_note_blocks {blocks, totalBlocks}; knowledge_search {evidence, sufficiency}; library_overview {files, totalFiles, processing}; read_pages {evidence, truncated}; propose_note_edits {changes}; web_search {results}; read_web_page {chars}; web_task {sources}. Show an unknown tool as a generic "Working…". Hidden tools (the final answer tools submit_answer and submit_questions) never emit events.

nextAfter.description: Pass as `after` on the next poll (the last seq returned, or your previous value).

done.description: True once the job is terminal; stop polling.

expiresAt.description: After this the job fails with AI_APPROVAL_EXPIRED.

stateVersion.description: The job’s `stateVersion` from when you showed the approval. A stale value is 409 AI_JOB_STATE_CHANGED: reload the job and its approvals.

headingPath.description: Headings above the passage, outermost first.

text.description: The passage exactly as the model saw it, copied when it was retrieved (it does not change if the Source is edited later). Untrusted user content: render as text.

remainingUsd.description: Estimated USD the user can still spend on AI today. A request needs headroom for its worst case, so a request can be refused before this reaches zero.

limitedBy.description: `global` means the whole service, not this user, is the binding limit.

resetsAt.description: Next UTC midnight, when the allowance resets.

kind.description: editText: new text for one block (nodeId, baseText, text). insertBlocks: new blocks at a position (position, blocks, texts). replaceBlocks: adjacent blocks swapped for new content (nodeIds, baseTexts, blocks, texts); when one block is replaced by one of the same type it keeps its ID, and so do nested blocks (list items, table rows and cells) that keep their position and type. deleteBlock and moveBlock: nodeId, baseText (and position for a move). Treat unknown kinds as not drawable and offer only Accept/Reject.

reason.description: Why a change is STALE: target_deleted, target_changed, overlapping_edit, anchor_deleted, invalid_position, not_text, or invalid_now (the result would not be a valid note, or an image the change adds was deleted since it was proposed).

undoable.description: An accepted change that can be undone.

nodeId.description: The block edited, deleted, or moved.

baseText.description: The block’s text when the agent read it (`\n` is a line break). Diff it against `text` to draw the change.

blocks.description: insertBlocks and replaceBlocks: the new canonical note blocks with their IDs — any block type the note supports that Markdown can express (paragraphs, headings, lists, checklists, tables, quotes, code, math with `latex`, rules, images by `assetId`), with marks (bold, italic, strike, code, http(s) links) and inline math. Render them read-only with the note renderer (math with KaTeX) as the preview; never insert them into the editor document. Links are not clickable until accepted.

texts.description: insertBlocks and replaceBlocks: the plain text of each new top-level block (fallback when a block cannot be drawn).

nodeIds.description: replaceBlocks: the blocks replaced, in document order.

baseTexts.description: replaceBlocks: the plain text of each replaced block when the assistant read it (for a strike-through or diff view).

jobId.description: The AI job that proposed it.

status.description: PROPOSED while any change is undecided; SUCCEEDED when at least one was accepted, REJECTED otherwise.

summary.description: One line from the assistant; plain text.

fromUntrusted.description: The assistant read web content before proposing: label it “includes web content”.

baseRevisionNumber.description: The note revision the assistant read.

accept.description: Change IDs to accept, applied in proposal order.

all.description: Accept all or reject all undecided changes; overrides `accept` and `reject`.

revisionNumber.description: The note revision that holds the accepted change.

currentRevisionNumber.description: The note head after the decision: load it (do not reapply the change locally).

title.description: Title shown to the learner. Defaults to the topic or the file name.

topic.description: What to quiz on, e.g. "B-tree page splits". Without it the quiz spreads over the outline of everything in scope.

questionTypes.description: Allowed types. Default single choice and true/false (about one in five). New types use full-match scoring without partial credit.

optionCount.description: Items per choice, matching or ordering question.

durationMinutes.description: Time limit in minutes. Omit for an untimed quiz.

options.description: Choice, matching or ordering items, alphabetical; no answer state.

cards.description: Flashcard fronts only; no backs. Slot IDs become stable cN IDs on publication.

reused.description: True when an existing artifact over the same material and options was returned instead of generating again (no charge).

preview.description: Validated batches so far, read-only. The final version may drop duplicates.

deck.description: Flashcard fronts and hints; reveal a back through the dedicated card endpoint.

questionIds.description: Questions of the current version to replace.

deadlineAt.description: Server deadline of a timed quiz.

questions.description: In this attempt’s order; option order is fixed per attempt.

answers.description: Answers by question ID: option ID, boolean, short text (max 800), ID array for multiple select/ordering, or blank/left ID to text/right ID map. Null clears. Type-specific bounds and membership are checked by the server.
Last answers to merge before grading (optional).

explanation.description: Null until its background explanation is ready; poll the result again.

explanationsComplete.description: False while some explanations are still being written.

cardTypes.description: itemCount counts facts. Each REVERSE fact creates two independently scheduled review cards; maximum 80 review cards.

expectedStateVersion.description: stateVersion from the due-card response; refresh it after a conflict.

description.example: Lecture notes and readings for the fall term.

retentionHold.description: True while a retention hold blocks deletion.

description.description: An empty string clears the description.

icon.description: An empty string clears the icon.

created.description: False when the Source was already linked (idempotent retry).

enabledByDefault.description: Whether AI context includes this Source by default.

priority.description: Higher priority Sources are listed and retrieved first.

version.description: Bumped on every change; mirrors room access idempotently.

email.description: The invited address. Present only to the note owner; null when the stored address cannot be decrypted.

invitations.description: Pending invitations. Emails are visible to the owner only.

email.description: The invited address. Present only to the note owner; null when the stored address cannot be decrypted.

token.description: Invitation token, returned once at creation. Empty on an idempotent replay: keep the first copy.

email.description: Address to share with. A verified Incantly user gets a grant at once; anyone else gets an invitation email.

role.description: VIEWER reads, COMMENTER reads and comments, EDITOR reads, comments and edits.

left.description: True when the grant holder left by themselves.

expiresAt.description: Optional expiry (ISO 8601), at most 365 days out. Defaults to 365 days when omitted: links always expire.

token.description: The link token, returned once. The public URL is GET /v1/shared/{token}.

note.description: Public note metadata (IDs and title only).

revision.description: The head revision record (no object keys).

document.description: The latest canonical Incantly JSON checkpoint, read-only.

noteId.description: The note to join live. Must already be shared; unshared notes use the note API.

token.description: The Liveblocks ID token. Expires after 1 hour; refresh through this endpoint.

roomId.description: The current room ID from the database. Always re-read it here: after a revocation rotation the room ID changes and the old connection is dropped.

userIds.description: Namespaced Liveblocks IDs (`user:…`, `agent:…`). At most 50; strangers are silently omitted.

avatarUrl.description: A stable application URL, or null when the user has none.

color.description: The stable cursor color for this user.

mode.description: Whether to connect to the room (`live`) or stay on saved sync. Call this before connecting.

reason.description: Why live is paused. Absent when `mode` is `live`. `NOT_SHARED`: the note is not shared. `GUARD_PAUSED`: the app-wide guard closed. `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`: the Free owner’s monthly budget is used.

resetsAt.description: When a budget or guard pause resets (ISO time).

roomId.description: The current room ID. Present when `mode` is `live`.

offlineEnabled.description: Whether the client may enable Liveblocks offline persistence. Gate offline mode on this flag; never enable it locally ahead of the server.

collabMode.description: Which realtime writer the client must construct for this note (`legacy`: the noteSync send path; `yjs`: the canonical fold — never both). The server decides from COLLAB_YJS_ENABLED plus the note allowlist; the client never decides alone. Always `legacy` until the Yjs rollout begins.

threadId.description: Reply into this thread. Omit to start a new thread (with `anchor`). Unknown threads are 404 THREAD_NOT_FOUND.

paragraphs.description: Paragraphs of inlines (`text`, `mention`, `link`). Limits: 50 paragraphs, 100 inlines each, 4000 characters total, 20 mentions.

anchor.description: Thread anchor metadata for a new thread (bounded string/number/boolean values, at most 16 keys). Ignored on replies.

payload.description: IDs only (noteId, grantId, actorUserId, …). Resolve titles through authorized reads.

emailEnabled.description: Email for all collaboration mail. False stops every collaboration email but keeps the in-app inbox.

muted.description: True when email for the scope is muted.

token.description: The signed token. May also arrive as `?token=` (one-click POST posts to the full URL).

List-Unsubscribe.description: Sent by mailbox providers on one-click unsubscribe; ignored.

cookieSession.name: better-auth.session_token
cookieSession.description: HttpOnly session cookie; production may use a secure-prefixed name. Never copy the token into JavaScript.
